explanation: Your usage: about {monthlyUnits} units (kWh) a month, which is about {monthlyBill} a month at an average rate of {tariff} per unit.
In {city}, one kW of panels on a {roof} makes about {yieldPerKw} units a month. We assume {sunHours} peak sun hours a day and {efficiency}% overall system efficiency.
To cover about {offset}% of your usage you need roughly {rawKw} kW. We round up to a standard size: {sizeKw} kW.
Cost: {sizeKw} kW at {pricePerKw} per kW, adjusted for {city} and your roof type, plus {fixedCharges} of fixed charges. We show a range of {costLow}% to {costHigh}% of that figure.
Savings: the system makes about {generatedUnits} units a month. We value the units you no longer buy at {tariff} each and show {savingsLow}% to {savingsHigh}% of that.
Payback: system cost divided by yearly savings. The short end pairs the lowest cost with the highest saving; the long end pairs the highest cost with the lowest saving.

faq.a: Net metering lets eligible solar customers send extra electricity to the grid and receive a credit on their bill. The rules and approval steps are set by the electricity distribution company and the regulator, and they can change, so we confirm the current process at your site survey.

Solar panels, inverters, cameras and recorders normally carry manufacturer warranties, and the terms differ by brand and product. Your written quotation lists the warranty for each item so you know what is covered.

Solar panels need regular cleaning and an occasional check of the inverter and wiring. CCTV needs clean lenses, a quick check that every camera is recording, and a look at the hard disk. We explain the routine when we hand over the system.
It depends on the system size, roof or building access and equipment availability. After the site survey we give you an expected schedule in the quotation.
No. It gives a range based on typical conditions. The final price is confirmed after a free site survey, when we see your roof, wiring and building.
